newsitem.title: USA: ComEd confident in its nuclear units safety.
newsitem.headline: ComEd confident in its nuclear units safety.

text.p: Unicom Corp's Commonwealth Edison Co on Wednesday reiterated that it will increase spending on its nuclear operations and is confident it will prove it can run its facilities safely.

At a news conference held in response to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission's addition of two more ComEd facilities to its watch list, James O'Connor, chief executive and chairman of ComEd, said the company already has a plan in place.
"We will be expending greater resources than we did a year ago, and those expenditures will increase or stay at those levels through the year 1998," O'Connor said.
"We anticipate they will drop in the years after that because much of what we are doing will be completed," he said.
ComEd said Wednesday it would increase its nuclear operating budget in 1997 to $1.2 billion, up 11 percent from 1996.

It also said it would begin immediately to respond to the NRC's request for ComEd to provide within 60 days "information under oath or affirmation explaining why NRC should have confidence in the company's ability to operate six nuclear stations while improving performance at each site".
O'Connor said the NRC did make favorable remarks about its progress with its Dresden nuclear facility, which was previously on the watch list. But it wanted further demonstration.

"He (the NRC representative) suggested, however, that we have not had the level of execution thus far that says we are a world-class nuclear operating company for all of our facilities," O'Connor said. "But I do think we are on the right trajectory."

O'Connor said its three facilities on the list -- Dresden and the newly added LaSalle and Zion operations -- are more than 25 years old and require attention and work. The company has a total of 12 nuclear plants, he said.
Although the company's plan of action for its nuclear facilities dates as far back as 1994, O'Connor said change takes time.

"What we're saying to the investors in our company is that we can return all of these plants to a position of top performance, which will lead to a lower cost production on a kilowatt hour basis, which over time will serve them very, very well," he said.
"It's not going to happen overnight, however," O'Connor said.
